Commander night at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda, Friday 28 August. Three-player pod: me, Alex, Stuart. Game four of four, and the only win of the night. Funniest game of the year.

Ramped through the early removal. The table spent its wipes on my mid-tier dinosaurs and I rebuilt faster than they could answer, which meant that when my board was empty I could fire BLASPHEMOUS ACT to clear THEIRS at no cost to me. That asymmetry was the whole game.

Then Gishath. Swung at Stuart for 7, revealed 7 cards off the trigger, hit FIVE dinosaurs — one of which makes their creatures enter tapped, so the board could not stabilise.

Next turn I drew Enlarge: +7/+7 on Gishath, swinging for 14 into Stuart's existing 7 commander damage = 21 and lethal by commander damage. Revealed 14 off that trigger, hit 2 more dinosaurs, one of which refilled my hand.

THE TABLE MISJUDGED THREAT TIERS. They spent their wraths on mid-tier dinosaurs and had nothing left when the commander landed. The deck's actual threat is the commander and the trigger, and my mid-tier bodies were effectively soaking removal for it.

No changes. This is the deck working as designed.

Alex's house, 4-player pod. Players: Sean, Alex, Oliver, Tom. Two games. Record: 0-2.

Game 2 — Gishath, Sun's Avatar (Naya dinos) (loss to Oliver / vampire drain)

Pod: Gishath (Sean), Vito (Oliver), Azorius counters (Alex), Aloro life gain (Tom). 2.5–3 hours, wipe after wipe.

Turn one: land, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet — four mana. Then green-screwed for a long stretch; hand full of double-green dinos, Selvala, Rishkar's Expertise.
The screw accidentally kept creatures off the table through the early wipe waves.
Gishath online once green arrived. Pumped +1 and doubled → 16/16, hit Tom for 16 commander damage on top of his 7 = dead. Revealed 16, hit two dinos (third/fourth reveal of the game — board was already stormed).
Had a no-attack deal with Oliver; had to break it to kill Tom because Tom's board would have wiped Sean otherwise. Stand by it.
Cast Zakama (7 with Urza's Incubator discount), swung Swords to Plowshares at the right time on open mana. Alex claimed Sean should have announced the life-gain mode — not the table standard; if he had a counter, that's on him.
Zakama vs. Walking Ballista back-and-forth; Ballista went down, life back to 13. Game effectively won.
Critical error: 8–9 dinos with counters, 30+ power on board, Alex at 18 and Oliver at 15. Should have swung everything at both — Alex saves himself, Oliver dies. Instead attacked only Oliver, Alex saved him, Oliver drained Sean out with a gain/lose/damage vampire spell.
Sean and Tom left; Alex and Oliver kept playing.

Lessons

Close lethal when it's on the board — hesitation cost the game.
Audit green pip distribution / green sources in the Gishath mana base.
In removal-heavy games, holding creatures back through wipe waves is a real strategy, not just an accident.
Enrage engine in Gishath is idling — too few ping sources to activate it; better fit for Standard than Commander.

Summary (both games): Both decks did what they were built to do and played at or above the table. Errors are getting fewer and more specific — the tuning has moved from "rebuild the deck" to "sequence and close better." Alex was salty in the morning text thread; that's a sign of being a real threat.

Follow-ups: Gishath: green mana base audit; reconsider the enrage package. Piloting: protect planeswalkers; swing lethal when it's there.
